INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT 19
====

EXAM BODY: KJSEA
GRADE: Grade 8 JSS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30

INSTRUCTIONS
----
• Answer all questions.
• For calculations, show full working (formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units).
• Diagrams provided are part of the question — use every labeled value.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A learner writes calcium as CA. What is the correct symbol and rule? (1 mark)
   A. Ca — first letter capital, second letter small
   B. CA — both letters must be capitals
   C. ca — both letters must be small
   D. C — calcium uses only one letter

2. Why is table salt (NaCl) classified as a compound? (1 mark)
   A. It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio
   B. It is white and looks pure
   C. It melts when heated
   D. It is mined at Lake Magadi only

3. In osmosis, what mainly moves across a selectively permeable membrane? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Sand grains
   C. Whole sugar crystals only
   D. Electric current

4. Eyepiece ×10 and objective ×10. What is total magnification? (1 mark)
   A. ×100
   B. ×20
   C. ×10
   D. ×20

5. Calculate pressure when F = 120 N and A = 0.5 m². (1 mark)
   A. 240 Pa
   B. 60 Pa
   C. 120.5 Pa
   D. 0.004166666666666667 Pa

6. The main energy chain in a simple torch is: (1 mark)
   A. Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)
   B. Light → chemical → sound
   C. Sound → nuclear → light
   D. Heat → food → electricity only

7. Iron has symbol Fe from the Latin name: (1 mark)
   A. Ferrum
   B. Natrium
   C. Aurum
   D. Kalium

8. Which statement correctly defines an element? (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical or physical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A substance that always conducts electricity

9. A learner writes calcium as CA. What is the correct symbol and rule? (1 mark)
   A. Ca — first letter capital, second letter small
   B. CA — both letters must be capitals
   C. ca — both letters must be small
   D. C — calcium uses only one letter

10. Why is table salt (NaCl) classified as a compound? (1 mark)
   A. It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio
   B. It is white and looks pure
   C. It melts when heated
   D. It is mined at Lake Magadi only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED QUESTIONS
----
11. Differentiate an element from a compound. Give one Kenyan example of each. (5 marks)

12. Explain why melting ice is a physical change but burning paper is a chemical change. (6 marks)

13. Explain why melting ice is a physical change but burning paper is a chemical change. (6 marks)

14. A force of 220 N acts on an area of 0.5 m². Calculate the pressure. Show full working. (8 marks)

pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. Correct option: A — Ca — first letter capital, second letter small

2. Correct option: A — It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio

3. Correct option: A — Water

4. Correct option: A — ×100
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective
2. Substitute values: Total = 10 × 10
3. Total = 100
Final Answer: ×100
Marks: M1 multiply; A1 answer

5. Correct option: A — 240 Pa
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: P = F / A
2. Substitute values: P = 120 / 0.5
3. P = 240
Final Answer: 240 Pa
Marks: M1 substitute; A1 Pa

6. Correct option: A — Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)

7. Correct option: A — Ferrum

8. Correct option: A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical or physical means

9. Correct option: A — Ca — first letter capital, second letter small

10. Correct option: A — It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio

11. (5 marks)
An element is a pure substance of one kind of atom and cannot be broken down chemically/physically into simpler substances (e.g. copper in wires, Fe in a jembe). A compound is made when different elements join chemically in fixed proportions (e.g. NaCl table salt, H₂O).

12. (6 marks)
Melting ice: still H₂O, no new substance, reversible by freezing → physical. Burning paper: ash/gases form, new substances, not simply reversible → chemical.

13. (6 marks)
Melting ice: still H₂O, no new substance, reversible by freezing → physical. Burning paper: ash/gases form, new substances, not simply reversible → chemical.

14. (8 marks)
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: P = F / A
2. Substitute values: P = 220 / 0.5
3. P = 440
Final Answer: 440 Pa
Marks: M1 formula/substitution; A1 final answer with Pa
